name: Boulby Underground Laboratory
notes: This map is thin: it can draw the mine's surface works site (traced from aerial imagery) and a sourced depth for the underground level, but no source consulted locates the specific shaft or the underground laboratory workings within that surface footprint. No detector is placed at site:boulby-mine in the Atlas (ZEPLIN and DRIFT, which the laboratory has hosted, are not yet Atlas entities), so no entity besides the site itself needs accounting here.

The two primary shaft collars (OSM 'Man Shaft (Downcast)' and 'Rock Shaft (Upcast)') and two shaft-head buildings are drawn. The mine's surface boundary is an OSM landuse outline. The underground laboratory itself is not drawn.

summary.plain: The Boulby potash mine in Redcar and Cleveland, north-east England, whose shafts lead down 1.1 km to the Boulby Underground Laboratory. The map shows the mine's surface works, the two primary shaft collars and two shaft-head buildings; the underground laboratory is not located.
summary.technical: OSM surface works outline, shaft collars and shaft-head buildings (georeferenced); 1.1 km shaft depth and 2840 m.w.e. from the AION workshop summary and DarkSPHERE paper; laboratory workings unlocated.

unlocated.backlog: A Boulby mine plan or STFC laboratory site plan with a scale, a paper that states the laboratory's distance from the shaft bottom (ZEPLIN/DRIFT/BUGS detector papers), or the STFC feasibility study for the new ~30 000 m3 facility; with a shaft-bottom offset and a bearing the main hall can be drawn at the 1.1 km level.
unlocated.reason: The laboratory is described only by depth and volume: 'at a depth of 1100 m, equivalent to 2840 m of water' with a 4000 m3 experimental space (main hall and Large Experimental Cavern, built 2015) and a planned ~30 000 m3 facility 'close to the current laboratory'. No fetched source gives its horizontal position or its distance and bearing from the two 1.1 km shafts, and OpenStreetMap carries no underground workings.
